title: Location: Road Names, Parking Lots & GPS
citation: NJTR-1 Crash Report Manual (2023), Appendix: General Questions
key_points: Locate private property and parking lot crashes by street address, followed by "parking lot."
Direction in box 10 is only for divided roads and one-way streets.
Latitude and longitude go in decimal degrees, not degrees, minutes and seconds.

faq.q: When do I fill in the direction in box 10?
faq.a: Only for divided roadways and one-way streets.

faq.q: A parking lot borders several streets. What address do I use?
faq.a: Use the lot's own street address from the municipal tax map or 9-1-1 database. If there isn't one, use a common name for the place, like "Whiting Lake (parking lot)."

faq.q: For a private property crash, do I list a cross street?
faq.a: No. Use the street address in box 10, followed by "parking lot" if it happened in a lot, for example "101 Main Street (parking lot)."

faq.q: Can an overpass be the nearest cross street?
faq.a: Yes. Overpasses, underpasses and railroad crossings can all be used.

faq.q: Do I need to fill in latitude and longitude?
faq.a: Fill them in if your department has GPS. Use decimal degrees only. NJDOT also relies on an accurate distance to the nearest cross road to place the crash.

faq.q: A car hits a curb. Is that private property?
faq.a: No. Curbing is part of the roadway system unless the whole crash happened on private or other off-road property.
